record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: Define a satisfactory notion of penalty functions and penalty-based functions on the lattice L([0,1]) of closed subintervals of [0,1], in a way that still recovers averaging aggregation operators on that lattice as penalty-based functions. The definition should handle the order structure of L([0,1]), including the partial order [a,b] <=_L [c,d] iff a<=c and b<=d, and possibly also linear admissible orders extending that partial order.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 (H. Bustince, J. Fernandez, M. Pagola, D. Paternain, E. Barrenechea). To define properly penalty functions and penalty-based functions in the lattice of closed subintervals of the unit interval [0, 1], L([0, 1]), in such a way that averaging aggregation operators in this lattice can be recovered as penalty-based functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L([0,1]) = \{[a,b] : 0 \le a \le b \le 1\}$ denote the set of closed subintervals of the unit interval, equipped with the componentwise partial order $[a,b] \le_L [c,d] \iff a \le c$ and $b \le d$, which makes $(L([0,1]),\le_L)$ a complete bounded lattice with bottom $[0,0]$ and top $[1,1]$. A linear order $\preceq$ on $L([0,1])$ is called admissible if it is a total order refining $\le_L$ (i.e., $[a,b] \le_L [c,d]$ implies $[a,b] \preceq [c,d]$).

Recall that on $[0,1]$, an aggregation function $F:[0,1]^n \to [0,1]$ is averaging if $\min(x_1,\dots,x_n) \le F(x_1,\dots,x_n) \le \max(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ for all inputs, and a penalty-based function associated with a penalty $P:[0,1]^{n+1}\to[0,\infty)$ is defined by $F(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\min_{y \in [0,1]} P(\mathbf{x},y)$ (with a suitable tie-breaking rule), where $P$ satisfies: (i) $P(\mathbf{x},y) \ge 0$, (ii) $P(\mathbf{x},y) = 0$ whenever $x_1 = \cdots = x_n = y$, (iii) $P(\mathbf{x},\cdot)$ is quasi-convex in $y$ for every fixed $\mathbf{x}$. It is a classical fact that every averaging aggregation function on $[0,1]$ can be represented as a penalty-based function.

Problem: Formulate a satisfactory definition of a penalty function $P:L([0,1])^{n+1}\to[0,\infty)$ and the corresponding notion of a penalty-based function $F:L([0,1])^n \to L([0,1])$, compatible with the lattice order $\le_L$ (and, if appropriate, with admissible linear orders $\preceq$ refining $\le_L$), such that every averaging aggregation operator on $(L([0,1]),\le_L)$ — i.e., every function $F:L([0,1])^n \to L([0,1])$ satisfying $\bigwedge_i X_i \le_L F(X_1,\dots,X_n) \le_L \bigvee_i X_i$ — can be recovered as a penalty-based function in this sense.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work by Bustince, Beliakov, and collaborators has addressed standard and quasi-penalty function definitions on $[0,1]$ and penalty-based aggregation on intervals (including non-convex intervals), but no source clearly establishes a fully satisfactory penalty/penalty-based framework on the lattice $L([0,1])$ that recovers all averaging aggregation operators there. The status of this specific formulation problem is not conclusively settled by available sources.

status_evidence.title: On the definition of penalty functions in data aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: A new standard definition of penalty functions is proposed that overcomes problems in different definitions in the literature, including a discussion of quasi-penalty functions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines penalty function definitions on [0,1], but does not explicitly settle the L([0,1]) lattice formulation.

status_evidence.title: A penalty-based aggregation operator for non-convex intervals
status_evidence.snippet: Existing extensions of averaging aggregation functions to inputs expressed as non-convex intervals are proposed, and an alternative aggregation operator is created using a novel penalty function.
status_evidence.claim: Penalty-based interval aggregation is partially developed, but a complete L([0,1]) penalty-based framework recovering all averaging operators is not established.

status_evidence.title: Averages on Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies averaging aggregation on lattices including L([0,1]).
status_evidence.claim: Treats averaging on lattices but does not provide the requested penalty-based characterization.
